name: Sokoto
summary_text: Sokoto's Sharia Penal Code Law took effect 31 January 2001 and prescribes stoning to death for married or previously married offenders convicted of consensual same-sex sexual activity (100 lashes where unmarried), with ta'azir discretionary punishment (up to 100 lashes and/or imprisonment) extending to same-sex acts between women and to cases involving a minor. This is the most capital-heavy statutory text within the twelve-state Sharia block. Hisbah religious-police activity is documented in Sokoto. USCIRF's 2019 case-level study covers Sokoto alongside Kano and Zamfara. Score 0.054 below the national 0.08, driven by the explicit death-by-stoning text and documented Sharia-court caseload. Tied with Kano: Kano pairs death text with the most active Hisbah; Sokoto pairs the stoning text directly with USCIRF case evidence. Both are above Bauchi, where a stoning sentence was actually carried out.

sources.claim_summary: Equaldex log entry #14118: the Sharia Penal Code Laws took effect in Sokoto on 31 January 2001; male same-sex activity is punished by stoning to death where the offender is or has been married, and 100 lashes otherwise; sexual acts between women (wsafa) draw ta'azir punishment of up to 100 lashes and/or imprisonment.
